newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks open hinges on Q4 ECI.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks open hinges on Q4 ECI.

text.p: Wall Street stocks and bonds will take their cue this morning from the fourth-quarter employmemnt cost index, a gauge closely watched by the U.S. Federal Reserve.

Analysts said that if the ECI figure, due at 0830 EST/1330 GMT, rose more than the forecast 0.9 percent, it would heighten the chances of an interest rate hike by the Fed coming sooner rather than later.
"The data will lead bonds and the bond market will lead stocks," one analyst said.
The analyst, Westfalia Investments director of research Peter Cardillo, said that the majority of investors usually did not pay much attention to this indicator.
"Usually, most people have no idea what this indicator is about," Cardillo said. "But a lot of attention is being given to it now because of the present situation with low unemployment levels."
Shares of ITT Corp are expected to surge at the opening after Hilton Hotels Corp announced on Monday it had offered the company for $55 a share.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei Average was up 461.67 points, or 2.66 percent, at 17,796.57.
In London, the FTSE 100 Index was down 8.5 at 4203.5.

Among U.S. shares traded in London, International Business Machines Corp was up 1/2 at 145-7/8, Digital Equipment Corp was up 1/8 at 36-3/4 and Intel Corp gained 1/2 to 15-5/8. Philip Morris Cos Inc shares were down 1/4 at 115-7/8.
The dollar was firm in Tokyo after moving above 120 yen and hit new highs against the mark in Europe.
U.S. Treasuries were mostly higher, with the long bond up 7/32 to yield 6.93 percent.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street writes that traders are talking about coming cuts in production by South Korean manufacturers of memory chips known as DRAMs, short for dynamic random access memory.
The rumors have pushed up shares of Micron Technology Inc and Texas Instruments Inc over the last two trading days.

The New York Times Market Place writes if CVS Corp acquires Revco D.S. Inc the deal would create the largest drugstore in a once sleepy industry that is becoming rapidly dominated by giant chains. The two companies confirmed yesterday that they were in merger talks but said the deal might not be completed.
